fields.before: An **alternating Turing machine** is a nondeterministic Turing machine whose non-halting states are partitioned into *existential* and *universal* states. A configuration is *accepting* if it is in an accepting state, or if it is existential and **some** successor configuration is accepting, or if it is universal and **all** successors are accepting (least fixed point, so infinite branches do not accept). The machine accepts $x$ if the start configuration is accepting. $\mathrm{ATIME}(t(n))$ and $\mathrm{ASPACE}(s(n))$ are the languages decided within the bounds on every branch. A machine with only existential states is an ordinary NTM; one with only universal states accepts exactly the complements of NTM languages.
fields.after: An **alternating Turing machine** is a nondeterministic Turing machine whose non-halting states are partitioned into *existential* and *universal* states. A configuration is *accepting* if it is in an accepting state, or if it is existential and **some** successor configuration is accepting, or if it is universal and **all** successors are accepting (least fixed point, so infinite branches do not accept). The machine accepts $x$ if the start configuration is accepting. $\mathrm{ATIME}(t(n))$ and $\mathrm{ASPACE}(s(n))$ are the languages decided within the bounds on every branch. A machine with only existential states uses ordinary NTM acceptance. For a finitely branching machine that halts on every branch on every input, swapping accepting/rejecting halts and existential/universal kinds complements its language. Under a uniform polynomial time bound on every branch, existential-only and universal-only machines characterize NP and coNP respectively. Without all-branch halting, the least-fixed-point convention does not give that complementation rule.

fields.before:
The computation tree is evaluated like a game tree: an existential node is an OR over its children, a universal node an AND, and halting leaves are the constants accept/reject (this is the NTM of toc-7.6 with the "some branch" rule applied only at $\exists$ states). The accepting computation is therefore not a path but a **subtree**: one child at each $\exists$ node and all children at each $\forall$ node. With all states existential the subtree is a single path (a certificate, NP); with all universal there is no choice and the machine accepts when every branch does (coNP); alternating the two kinds gives $\Sigma_k$ and $\Pi_k$ by running $k$ blocks of existential/universal states (3.5) — and, as 3.9 and 3.10 show, unbounded alternation reaches PSPACE and P.

For the complementation comparison, fix an input x and require finite branching and halting on every computation branch. The contrapositive of König's lemma (logic 2.10) makes the unfolded computation tree finite: an infinite finitely branching tree would have an infinite branch. Induction on this finite tree then gives the De Morgan duality: swap existential and universal nodes and interchange accepting and rejecting leaves, and each node's Boolean value is negated. In particular an all-universal decider complements the corresponding all-existential decider with swapped halting labels. A looping branch blocks this finite-tree argument; the least-fixed-point convention does not make looping reject in one machine and accept in its dual. Inputwise finiteness alone supplies no polynomial running-time bound.

The computation tree is evaluated like a game tree: an existential node is an OR over its children, a universal node an AND, and halting leaves are the constants accept/reject (this is the NTM of toc-7.6 with the "some branch" rule applied only at $\exists$ states). For $k\ge1$, at most k quantifier blocks beginning existentially or universally give $\Sigma_k$ or $\Pi_k$ under that polynomial-time bound (3.5). Unbounded alternation within polynomial time gives PSPACE (3.9), while alternating logarithmic space gives P with the stated decider convention (3.10). These claims do not assign those classes to arbitrary unbounded machines. A single non-halting self-loop has no accepting configuration in the least fixed point, and swapping its node kind still leaves it nonaccepting; thus naive dualization cannot complement arbitrary looping machines.

Induction on this finite tree then gives the De Morgan duality: swap existential and universal nodes and interchange accepting and rejecting leaves, and each node's Boolean value is negated. In particular an all-universal decider complements the corresponding all-existential decider with swapped halting labels. A looping branch blocks this finite-tree argument; the least-fixed-point convention does not make looping reject in one machine and accept in its dual. Inputwise finiteness alone supplies no polynomial running-time bound.
